title: US Labor Department Launches Sweeping H-1B Fraud Probe With Dozens of Subpoenas
excerpt: Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito says investigators are tracking visa fraud tied to labor trafficking and criminal gangs, with Cognizant named in whistleblower discussions.
body:
• The DOL Office of Inspector General opened a nationwide investigation into H-1B and PERM visa fraud on July 8, 2026, issuing dozens of subpoenas.
  • Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito linked visa fraud to labor trafficking, cartels, and transnational gangs, calling it the most aggressive action by an IG in this administration.
  • The probe is part of Project Firewall, which has opened more than 175 investigations into visa program abuses since September 2025.

The Trump administration has launched its first major investigation into alleged fraud in the H-1B and PERM visa programs, marking a significant escalation in the government's crackdown on employment-based immigration abuses.

Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito announced the probe on July 9, telling Fox Business that investigators had already begun issuing dozens of subpoenas to companies and labor brokers suspected of manipulating the visa system.

"Without a doubt, we are going to take what we believe is probably the most aggressive action against foreign labor fraud by an Inspector General in this administration. We've already started to issue dozens of subpoenas."

— Anthony D'Esposito, DOL Inspector General

Beyond Paperwork Violations

D'Esposito framed the investigation as far more than a compliance review. He said visa fraud was fueling violent crime and that much of the trafficking connected to foreign labor programs was tied to cartels and transnational gangs.

"This is not just people working in factories," D'Esposito said. "These are people working in medical facilities and doctors' offices that are actually putting people in harm's way."

The inspector general also said whistleblowers had raised concerns involving large technology firms. He named Cognizant as part of the investigation's current discussions, though no formal charges have been filed against the company. Roughly 65 percent of all H-1B visa holders work in the technology sector.

Project Firewall Expands

The inquiry is part of Project Firewall, a multi-agency initiative launched in September 2025 to increase oversight of employment-based visa programs. Since its launch, the Labor Department has opened more than 175 investigations into abuses across visa programs.

Vice President JD Vance announced the broader anti-fraud strategy during an event in Milwaukee on the same day. "American jobs ought to go to American workers and not foreign fraudsters, and the Department of Labor is fighting back against it," Vance said.

The DOL Office of Inspector General posted on X: "We're issuing subpoenas, tracking every lead, and putting criminals in cuffs. Teaming up with @POTUS & @VP's @WHFraudTF to put American workers first."

Shift to Proactive Audits

The administration has moved away from complaint-driven reviews toward proactive enforcement. Under the new model, the Secretary of Labor can initiate audits based on "reasonable cause" alone, lowering the threshold for federal scrutiny.

Employers now face a more intrusive compliance environment. Companies can draw unannounced site visits and online presence reviews. Firms found out of compliance risk removal from the H-1B program, civil penalties, and criminal charges.

Starting July 10, 2026, USCIS began rejecting any application filed with auto-generated or copy-pasted signatures, adding another compliance hurdle for employers and immigration attorneys.

Impact on Indian IT Workers

The investigation carries particular weight for the Indian diaspora. Indians account for an estimated 71 percent of all approved H-1B applications in recent years, and Indian IT services firms have historically been among the largest users of the program.

The probe comes alongside a new wage-weighted H-1B selection system that took effect on February 27, 2026, replacing the random lottery. The system favors higher-paid applicants, with Wage Level IV receiving four entries compared to one for Level I.

A federal court struck down the administration's $100,000 H-1B application fee in June 2026, but the government has said it will appeal. Combined with the fraud investigation, these measures represent a fundamental reshaping of how foreign workers enter and remain in the US labor market.

What Comes Next

D'Esposito's office has signaled that the investigation will not stop with a single company or a narrow document review. The inspector general said investigators would follow "every lead," language that signals an expanding review across employers, intermediaries, and recruiting pipelines.

For Indian professionals on H-1B visas and those seeking new sponsorship, the tightening enforcement environment adds uncertainty to an already competitive process. Foreign workers can be caught in delayed filings, rejected applications, or employer investigations that affect work authorization and green card timelines, even without any allegation against them personally.
